description:
(Summary from jobright.ai; the original posting may say more.)

TriNet is hiring a Software Engineer to develop, test, and release web and mobile applications. The role contributes to new and existing solutions across the software development lifecycle, including testing, debugging, automation, and releases.
Software engineer developing, testing, debugging, and prototyping application solutions

Responsibilities:
• Participate in the design and development of new solutions as well as in enhancements and updates to existing solutions along with fixing the issues in the system
• Contribute to the software development life cycle, focusing on development, testing, troubleshooting and debugging software solutions
• Contribute to the best coding practices and help with code merges and releases
• Develop unit and automation test scripts under the test-driven development lifecycle
• Leverage AI coding assistants for code generation, review, and test creation
• Build rapid prototypes and proof-of-concepts (POCs) to validate new ideas and solutions

Requirements:
• Understanding of all phases of Software development life cycle
• Experience building UIs with React (components, hooks, state, forms)
• Working knowledge of JavaScript or TypeScript, including building server-side APIs with Node.js. Coursework, internships, bootcamps and personal projects all count
• Familiarity with microservice architecture, end-to-end UI/API integration, API protocols like REST and graphQL
• Experience writing automated tests (Jest, React Testing Library or similar)
• Hands-on use of AI-assisted coding tools (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Codex or similar)

Preferred:
• Bachelor's degree in computer science/engineering or related field or equivalent experience
• 0–2 years of experience and prior internship or coursework experience recommended
• Solid SQL and relational database fundamentals (schema design, joins, migrations)
• PostgreSQL preferred
• Coming from Java, C#, Python or another stack? We welcome it. Show us the JavaScript or TypeScript you've written, even a side project
